title: PHP2Shell - quick mitigation pre-patch
description: A use-after-free (UAF) vulnerability exists in PHP's session.upload_progress handler related to serialize-state cross-request handling. This vulnerability does not lead to remote code execution but can cause memory safety issues and arbitrary memory reads/writes. The vulnerability affects prefork-based PHP setups and is confirmed with a medium severity impact. A pre-patch mitigation is available by disabling session.upload_progress in PHP configuration. Official patches are expected in PHP versions 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.11.

references.title: Reddit Discussion: PHP2Shell - quick mitigation pre-patch

aiSummary: The PHP session.upload_progress feature contains a use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) involving the serialize-state cross-request handling in the session upload progress handler. The bug arises because the serialize/unserialize globals are not properly reset before PHP request initialization, leading to reuse of freed memory blocks and arbitrary memory read/write conditions. The cached-pointer path initially thought exploitable is confirmed dead, but the serialize-state UAF remains a real memory safety issue with a CVSS-equivalent severity of 5.3 (medium). This vulnerability affects prefork MPM with mod_php setups and requires specific heap grooming for exploitation. Disabling session.upload_progress in php.ini or .htaccess closes both vulnerable paths. Additional mitigation includes clamping multipart uploads at the network edge. Official patches are planned for PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.11.
aiImpact: The vulnerability allows use-after-free memory corruption leading to arbitrary memory read/write primitives but does not enable remote code execution. It can cause application crashes (SIGSEGV) and memory exhaustion. The impact is limited to prefork PHP setups with session.upload_progress enabled and is mitigated by disabling this feature. No active exploits in the wild are reported.
